title: Steve Gleason Act of 2015
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the Senate passed version is repeated here.)

Steve Gleason Act of 2015

(Sec. 2) This bill amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to cover as durable medical equipment any eye tracking and gaze interaction accessories for speech generating devices furnished to individuals with a demonstrated medical need for them.

(Sec. 3) Payment for speech generating devices or accessories shall be made on a rental basis, or in a lump-sum amount for the purchase of the item, without a cap on the amount in the case of devices furnished on or after October 1, 2015, and before October 1, 2018.

summary.headline: This law makes Medicare cover eye-tracking accessories for speech-generating devices for people who medically need them, with uncapped payments for devices furnished in a set window.
summary.what_it_does: The law amends the Medicare program to treat eye tracking and gaze interaction accessories for speech-generating devices as durable medical equipment. Coverage applies to people who have a demonstrated medical need for them. For devices furnished from October 1, 2015 through October 1, 2018, Medicare payment may be made on a rental basis or as a lump-sum purchase, and the payment has no dollar cap.

who_it_affects.group: Medicare beneficiaries who need speech-generating devices
who_it_affects.how: They can have eye-tracking and gaze interaction accessories covered by Medicare if they have a demonstrated medical need for them.

who_it_affects.group: Medicare beneficiaries who use speech-generating devices during the 2015 to 2018 window
who_it_affects.how: Payment for these devices and accessories may be made as a rental or lump sum with no cap on the amount for devices furnished in that period.

who_it_affects.group: Suppliers of durable medical equipment and speech-generating devices
who_it_affects.how: They can bill Medicare for eye-tracking and gaze interaction accessories under the rules for durable medical equipment.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted July 30, 2015. The no-cap payment rule applies to devices furnished on or after October 1, 2015 and before October 1, 2018.
